content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working on configuring [product_name] to send its input registers (I1-I16) to a Modbus TCP slave device using the VW address 1024 as referenced in the [product_name] software help. When I enter the address in the configuration table, I consistently get an out-of-range error. Is it possible to transfer all input registers as a word to the Modbus slave, or is it necessary to send each input bit separately to the coils? Thanks for any guidance.

Thanks for your response. This solution writes to coils in the slave device, not to holding registers. I should have clarified earlier—I want to transfer the data as a single register into the holding registers of the slave device.

There isn't a dedicated register for inputs on [product_name]. You can send the input statuses using network outputs in the VM word area, and then transfer this VM word to a holding register in the slave device.

It's not possible to access those VM area addresses (like 1024) within the [product_name] program itself. The program only allows VM addresses up to 850.7; higher addresses such as 1024 can be reached only from external devices.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced a limitation when trying to write grouped input statuses from [product_name] to a Modbus TCP slave using an address promoted in the [product_name] software. Direct access to higher VM addresses is not available within the program, limiting straightforward Modbus word transfers and requiring alternate methods.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to transfer all input statuses from [product_name] to a Modbus TCP slave's holding register as a single word by directly addressing as described in the software help.
